title: Development of an advanced biomaterial composed of acid‐modified cellulose‐rich corn (Zea mays) cob and crosslinked chitosan: Structural characterization and adsorption studies
content:
Abstract

In this study, an advanced biomaterial composed of sulfuric acid-modified cellulose-rich corn (Zea mays) cob and crosslinked chitosan-citrate was synthesized. The developed material (crosslinked chitosan/acid-modified cellulose-rich corn cob using sulfuric acid, CTS-CT/CC-H) was applied for the removal of a cationic dye (specifically, crystal violet, CV). The study used the Box–Behnken design to examine the impact of uptake variables: (A) CTS-CT/CC-H dosage (ranging from 0.02 to 0.08 g), (B) pH (ranging from 4 to 10), and (C) duration (ranging from 10 to 40 min) on the removal of CV. Using the desirability function of the Box–Behnken design, the optimal conditions for CV removal (90.3%) were achieved at a CTS-CT/CC-H dosage of 0.055 g, a solution pH of 9, and a contact time of 20.7 min. The kinetic and isotherm data showed that the Freundlich and pseudo-first-order models perfectly defined the uptake of CV by CTS-CT/CC-H. The CTS-CT/CC-H composite had an uptake ability of 466.8 mg/g for the CV dye. The uptake of CV dye onto the CTS-CT/CC-H composite is attributed to hydrogen bonding, electrostatic contact, and n-π stacking interaction. This study suggests that the CTS-CT/CC-H material is a very effective bioadsorbent that may be effectively used for dye wastewater treatment. The collected results also provide a sustainable and environmentally friendly way to produce efficient adsorbents for eliminating cationic dyes. This study highlights the potential of bio-based polymers as sustainable and efficient materials for wastewater treatment, promoting the valorization of agricultural residues in environmental remediation applications.
